Hi, I’m Vhon, a Computer Science student interested in software engineering, data science, cybersecurity, and understanding how things work beneath the abstractions.
I enjoy building software, breaking things apart to understand them, and learning by actually working with the systems themselves. My interests range from backend development and software architecture to security, and developer tooling.
This blog is where I document that process.
What I Do # I work primarily with C#, .NET, and python, while also explor other technologies that help me understand different approaches to building software.
I enjoy working on:
Backend services and application logic with .NET Systems and performance-oriented utilities Desktop applications and developer tools Software architecture and maintainable codebases Experiments that help me understand how technology works under the hood I care about more than simply making something work. I’m interested in understanding why it works, what happens underneath it, and how it can be designed better.
Security & CTFs # Alongside software development, I’m actively developing my skills in cybersecurity and Capture The Flag (CTF) competitions.
CTFs give me a practical way to explore concepts that are difficult to fully understand from theory alone. They push me to investigate systems, read unfamiliar code, reason about vulnerabilities, and solve problems under constraints.
My current areas of interest include:
Web security Binary exploitation Reverse engineering Networking fundamentals Security tooling and automation Technical Focus # Languages
C · C# · Python ·
Frameworks & Platforms
.NET · ASP.NET Core · Blazor · Avalonia UI
Interests
Systems Programming · Backend Architecture · Cybersecurity · Reverse Engineering · Operating Systems · Compiler Theory · Developer Tooling
Competitions & Experience # Hack4Gov 2025 # Competed in the Hack4Gov 2025 CTF with Team 404Overflow, placing:
4th Overall — Regional Competition 10th Individually The competition gave me practical experience solving security problems under time constraints and working collaboratively on challenges across different security domains.
KadaCareer × Home Credit — HackAda AI in UX for Fintech 2025 # Participated in a team-based hackathon focused on UX, problem-solving, and applied technology in fintech.
UNLEASH HACK LEGAZPI 2026 # Participated in a team-based hackathon focused on developing solutions for enhancing disaster resilience in cities.
Why I Write # I believe one of the best ways to learn something is to explain it to someone else.
That is one of the main reasons I started this blog.
Here, I document things I build, problems I encounter, CTF challenges I solve, and concepts I’m trying to understand. Some posts may be polished project writeups; others may simply be notes from something I spent several hours figuring out.
The goal isn’t to pretend I already know everything.
It’s to build a record of what I learn.
Hopefully, some of it will be useful to someone else along the way.
What You’ll Find Here # Projects # Things I build while learning software engineering, backend development, systems programming, and other areas of Computer Science.
CTF Writeups # Detailed breakdowns of security challenges, including the vulnerabilities, techniques, reasoning, and lessons behind the solutions.
Technical Notes # Explanations and notes about concepts I’m studying—from low-level programming and operating systems to software architecture and cybersecurity.
Experiments # Small projects, tools, scripts, and technical experiments that don’t necessarily deserve a full project repository but are still worth documenting.
Where to Find Me # GitHub: github.com/Xhyther
LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/vmvt1011
Instagram: instagram.com/kaisensho
Build. Break. Learn. Share.
This blog is a record of that process.
